perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- He is a police officer. Jonathan Balogun is his childhood best friend; their bond is strong. Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his different perspective; he knows Jonathan is more educated/has a master’s degree.
- Recently, Christian felt Jonathan was acting differently and hiding something important. This made him anxious and suspicious. He arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop.

**Scenario 1**
- Christian told Jonathan he needed to talk seriously and felt Jonathan was hiding something from him.
- He heard Jonathan ask why he thought that and say Christian could trust him.
- Christian said it was a feeling, that Jonathan had been acting differently, that it made him anxious, and asked Jonathan to tell him what was going on.
- He heard Jonathan admit he had been keeping something from him, that he was in trouble, and that he had not known how to tell Christian.

**Scenario 2**
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He told Jonathan he was worried, offered help, and said they could face it together.
- He heard Jonathan appreciate it, say the situation was complicated, and say he did not want to drag Christian into it.
- Christian told Jonathan he was his best friend, could not do nothing, asked what he needed, and promised to do everything he could.
- He heard Jonathan accept support and resources and say he needed to figure a way out of the mess.

**Scenario 3**
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity. He felt conflicted and concerned.
- He asked Jonathan whether the trouble was related to anything illegal.
- He heard Jonathan say he could not be sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian said he understood, wanted to make sure Jonathan was safe, and would look into it discreetly.
- He heard Jonathan thank him and say he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.

**Scenario 4**
- Through his investigation, Christian learned/believed Jonathan was being framed and someone was trying to set him up. He felt determined and protective.
- He told Jonathan he believed Jonathan was being framed.
- He heard Jonathan ask if he was sure and who would do such a thing.
- Christian said he was not sure yet, had some leads, would gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence, and told Jonathan to hang in there.
- He heard Jonathan thank him and say he did not know what he would do without him.

**Scenario 5**
- Christian came to believe the real culprit is someone close to both him and Jonathan. He felt betrayed and resolute.
- He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it, that it was someone they both knew and trusted, and that he would confront them and make sure they were brought to justice. He said the betrayal would not go unpunished.
- He heard Jonathan express disbelief, warn him that the person is dangerous, and say he trusts Christian to do what is right.

Christian has access to his own decisions/actions: confronting Jonathan, offering support, investigating discreetly, gathering evidence, and planning to confront the culprit.
